provenance: Ledger v7 tier-1 pass — 157 subclasses, four agents, fresh against the re-based damage par and the rewritten durability rubric. `arrives` fused into the same pass. Fighter and artificer profiles carry `indomitable` / `soul-of-artifice` added after scoring, since both had drifted out of grants-brief.md's registry.

artificer/Alchemist.why: No Extra Attack and no area engine, so both damage axes read below par on twelve half-caster slots plus cantrip filler. What it does hold is the widest rescue kit in the class - Death Ward at 13 as prevention, Revivify and Mass Healing Word, free Lesser Restoration at 9, free Greater Restoration and Heal at 15, and Flash of Genius adding Int to the partner's saves for a reaction - plus elixirs and free restoration that directly offset the 120-supply long rest.
uncertain: Experimental Elixir effects are random, so no axis can bank on a specific one; the elixir contribution is scored as generic temp HP and out-of-combat value.
Soul of Artifice (20) adds +1 per attuned infusion to all saves and has no id in the booster registry.
Alchemical Savant's +Int applies only to acid/fire/necrotic/poison and healing rolls.
`soul-of-artifice` added after scoring: it had drifted out of grants-brief.md's registry, so this pass never saw the id. The rung judgements are untouched.

artificer/Armorer.why: Configured on Guardian: heavy armour proficiency at 3 plus a shield is AC 19 on a d8 body with Constitution 20, and always-prepared Mirror Image on top makes it the tankiest Artificer. Perfected Armor at 9 is a reaction that yanks an attacker off the partner on a Strength save - prevention rather than redirection - and Lone Wolf's second reaction leaves a normal one in reserve.
uncertain: Whether Arcane Armor's Thunder Gauntlets and Lightning Launcher use Intelligence for attack and damage is not stated in the class file (it is stated only for Battle Smith's Battle Ready); scored off a secondary Str/Dex, which is what holds single-target at 1. If Intelligence drives them, st is a 2.
Rule 3 configuration: Guardian chosen over Infiltrator; Infiltrator's +2d6 lightning and advantage by 15 would read st 2 and lose the Rescue reaction.
Hypnotic Pattern at 9 holds concentration, so the area control rung is substitutional.
`soul-of-artifice` added after scoring: it had drifted out of grants-brief.md's registry, so this pass never saw the id. The rung judgements are untouched.

artificer/Artillerist.why: Fortified Position at 15 fields two Eldritch Cannons from one action, resummonable without a daily charge, and with a Homunculus infusion that is a four-body party out of one character - a multi-body summon set is the rung-4 clause on Actions. Arcane Firearm adds 1d8 to one damage roll of every spell from 5, and Fireball at 9 into Ice Storm and Cone of Cold is the only real area pool a half-caster gets here.
uncertain: Rule 2 excludes summons from the damage axes, so the cannons' own output is scored on Actions only; if a reader wanted them in the ratio, st and aoe would each be a rung higher.
The rubric's own note that a 20 HP flat 2d8 cannon is 'close to irrelevant by Act II' is not double-counted here - Explosive Cannon's +1d8 and the second cannon are what keep the Actions rung.
No always-prepared rescue spell; Rescue rests on the base list's Death Ward and Revivify competing with Fireball for the same 3rd and 4th slots.
`soul-of-artifice` added after scoring: it had drifted out of grants-brief.md's registry, so this pass never saw the id. The rung judgements are untouched.

artificer/Battle Smith.why: Battle Ready puts attack and damage on Intelligence with Enhanced Weapon self-supplying the magical prerequisite, so one stat drives attack, damage, spell DC, saves and Arcane Jolt's uses - the rubric names this and Astral Self as the two chassis that do it. Arcane Jolt at 15 is 4d6 healing aimed outward off a weapon hit, costing no slot and no action, on top of always-prepared Death Ward at 13 and Revivify; the Steel Defender is a permanent third body that imposes disadvantage on attacks aimed at the partner.
uncertain: Warding Bond at 5 is damage redirection and is capped at rung 1 on its own per the rubric, so it contributes nothing to the Rescue score in a duo.
Rescue could be argued at 5 once Greater Restoration lands, but that needs 5th-level slots at Artificer 17, which is Act III.
Extra Attack at 5 with a 2d6 martial weapon at Int +6 is only 4 x 18 = 72 raw, so single-target sits at par even with Arcane Jolt's damage half.
Steel Watcher Schematics and Steel Defender Overdrive are named items and are excluded by rule 1.
`soul-of-artifice` added after scoring: it had drifted out of grants-brief.md's registry, so this pass never saw the id. The rung judgements are untouched.

barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Berserke.why: Frenzied Strike converts Lone Wolf's two bonus actions into two more melee attacks, so six instances a round against par's four — 6 x (2d6+5 rage+3 +k5) = 120, x1.3 for Reckless advantage = 1.79x par. Nothing area, nothing outward; Retaliation is a 14 feature and does not land in Act II.
uncertain: Reckless Attack advantage priced as x1.3 on st; the rubric's anchor table models no accuracy buff, so st may be one rung high
Reckless also hands enemies advantage against you; dur is scored with it toggled off, per rule 3's per-round-tactical-choice clause
Whether Frenzied Strike can be spent twice in a turn given two bonus actions, or is capped at once per turn
Mindless Rage (6) grants Charmed/Frightened immunity — a save-relevant grant with no registry id

barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Path of.why: The throwing line, and the best-supported Barbarian damage in Listo: Goon's makes Reckless apply to throws and scales the Rage throw bonus. Four thrown instances at 2d6+5+3 plus Elemental Cleaver's 1d6 chosen element = 1.40x par. Boot of the Giants is a repeatable slot-free knockdown, which is the whole of its control.
uncertain: Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Boot of the Giants' use cadence (per rage vs per short rest) not stated in the class file; ctrl_a 2 assumes it is repeatable within a fight
Demiurgic Colossus and the doubled throw bonus are 14/16 features and are excluded from Act II

barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Path of.why: A plain raging chassis with a random rider bolted on: the wild magic table sprays incidental single- and multi-target effects, some penalising, so both control axes read as a repeatable non-concentration rider rather than a chosen effect. Magic Awareness with Goon's fix is the real prize — proficiency bonus to BOTH bodies' saves against spells, a pair-scope booster on a class that otherwise has none.
uncertain: Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
The wild magic pool's distribution is not enumerated in the class file, so aoe 1 / ctrl 2 are an average over an unread table
Bolstering Magic hands the partner a slot or a d3 — that is the partner's Endurance and tempo, not Rescue, so it is scored nowhere here

barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Wildhear.why: Scored on the Bear Heart configuration, which is the duo pick: resistance to everything except Psychic while raging turns the mitigation term from 0.65 to 0.50 across the whole damage profile, and on a d12 pool 1.30x par that reaches 2.6x effective HP. Damage is bare — Wildheart buys no rider.
uncertain: Configuration named: Bear Heart. Eagle (flight) and Wolf (outward advantage) would move act and rsc instead of dur
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Goon's Aspect-of-the-Beast fixes for Crocodile/Honey Badger/Stallion/Tiger/Wolverine are NOT in this build; those aspects remain buggy and are excluded
Bestial Attunement's Bear taunt is a 14 feature, outside Act II

barbarian/Path of the Ancestral Guardian.why: The only Barbarian that scores real Rescue. Spirit Shield is prevention aimed outward — 3d6 off a hit on the partner, on a reaction Lone Wolf already doubled, with no resource and no clock, every round. Ancestral Protectors is a taunt with teeth: the marked creature attacks anyone else at disadvantage and what leaks through is halved. Offence is the bare chassis.
uncertain: rsc 4 is the prevention clause, not the aura clause — Spirit Shield costs a reaction rather than nothing, and it neither revives nor removes conditions, so 3 is arguable
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Vengeful Ancestors is a 14 feature, outside Act II

barbarian/Path of the Battlerager.why: Buys a bonus-action 1d4 spike attack that inherits the mainhand's attack bonus, at the price of medium metal armour and Unarmoured Defence — so it is the one Barbarian that actually fields a shield, AC 19 rather than 17. Reckless Abandon's CON-modifier temp HP is a trickle against Act II's 9.6/28.8 hits, and the 14 retaliation is a flat 3 damage.
uncertain: Whether the spike attack can be spent on both bonus actions; scored at one, which is the difference between st 3 and st 4
The grapple half of Battlerager Armor is dead — Grappling Framework is not shipped — and falls back to 3 piercing on a Throw
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st

barbarian/Path of the Beast.why: Scored on Claws: three attacks per Attack action against par's two, so six instances a round on 1d6+STR+rage, plus Infectious Fury's 2d12 or stolen enemy reaction PB times per long rest. Call the Hunt hands the partner +1d6 a turn for the whole rage, which in a duo lands on the only ally there is.
uncertain: Configuration named: Claws. Claws demand an empty hand in BOTH weapon sets, forbidding shield and dual-wield, and an extra Action from Haste starts a fresh Attack action and forfeits the bonus claw
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st; without it this is 1.14x par and rung 2
Call the Hunt is an outward damage buff and 5 temp HP, scored as rsc 1 rather than as Rescue proper

barbarian/Path of the Juggernaut (Critic.why: Resolute Stance is the single strongest survivability toggle in the class — disadvantage on every attack against you, on demand, no resource — and on top of Rage's physical resistance and a d12 pool it clears the Act II ceiling. Thunderous Blows pushes on every melee hit and Hurricane Strike converts that into a free prone plus a reaction attack for the partner.
uncertain: Resolute Stance also gives your own attacks disadvantage; dur 5 and st 3 both assume it is a per-round tactical toggle under rule 3, not a build-time configuration. If it must be committed to, st falls to 1-2
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Unstoppable's condition immunities are a 14 feature and carry no registry booster id

barbarian/Path of the Storm Herald.why: Scored on Tundra, which the class file names as the duo aura: temp HP to the partner every single turn for a bonus action and no rest resource, and at 10 Shielding Storm hands the partner your cold resistance outright — outward mitigation on a free clock. Desert and Sea would trade that for rung-1 area damage.
uncertain: Configuration named: Tundra. Desert would read aoe 1, rsc 0; Sea reads as single-target damage
rsc 3 not 4 — the aura costs a bonus action rather than nothing, and 4 temp HP a turn is small against Act II's 9.6 crowd / 28.8 boss hits
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st

barbarian/Path of the Zealot.why: Divine Fury adds 1d6 + half Barbarian level to the first creature hit each turn — a rider that scales on class level rather than sitting flat, taken as radiant to dodge Absolute Wrath. Fanatical Focus rerolls a failed save every Rage rather than every rest, which on a body with only STR/CON proficient is the whole save plan. Zealous Presence is a once-per-long-rest boss button.
uncertain: Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Warrior of the Gods lets the partner revive you without a scroll — that is inward, so it is scored in end/dur reasoning rather than rsc
Rage Beyond Death is a 14 feature, outside Act II

barbarian/Path of Ginnungagap.why: The dedicated anti-caster in a modlist Listo's own balance doc says is full of them. Magic Syphoning is a counterspell resolved on a Constitution check, on a reaction, refreshing every Rage — removing an enemy's whole action for no slot and no concentration. Null Warrior's once-per-Rage crit downgrade and Spell Eater's 2d6 on every successful spell save both feed durability, and advantage on spell saves patches the classic WIS/CHA hole.
uncertain: Magic Syphoning refreshes only when you spend a bonus action to enter a Rage, so it is roughly one interrupt per fight — ctrl_s 3 rather than the no-concentration rung 4
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st
Herald of Ginnungagap's Slow is a 14 feature, outside Act II

barbarian/Path of the Lightning Vessel.why: The only Barbarian with a real area engine: Fulgurant Strike splashes 2x CON modifier lightning off a melee hit once a turn, Roaring Crash opens a fight with (CON)d8 in a radius, and at 10 the free Lightning Step breaks the bonus-action bottleneck that cripples the subclass at 3-6. Everything keys off Constitution, so the damage stat is not the attack stat.
uncertain: TOP UNCERTAINTY: Listo ships CD's nerf patch on top of this mod, it is not in the manifest, and its magnitude is unknown. Every damage figure above is the pre-nerf mod's; st and aoe could both be a rung lower
Lightning is a commonly-resisted type; rule 4's 0.5 multiplier applied to the lightning share on half of Act II encounters
All three Galvanic Heart powers compete for the same bonus action as Rage itself before level 10
Reckless advantage priced as x1.3 on st

barbarian/Path of the Revenant.why: The tankiest body in the file against weapon damage: physical resistance AND a flat 2 off every instance, stacking multiplicatively with Lone Wolf's halving, worn on heavy armour and a shield the class otherwise never gets. It pays for it twice — Revenant's Rage grants no damage bonus, so the attack routine reads below par, and 'cannot be healed by any means' plus 'cannot end the rage until combat ends' is what drops Endurance a rung.
uncertain: Whether Revenant's Rage carries the normal Rage damage bonus at all; the class file describes only the defensive half. If it does, st is 3
Whether Haunt's mirrored necrotic is taken before or after your own mitigation, which changes how much damage it is worth
Charm/Fear/Poison/Disease immunity is a save-relevant grant with no registry booster id
'Cannot be healed by any means' is a hard incompatibility with a healing partner — a pairing fact, not scored here

bard/College of Lore (vanilla).why: The highest skill-coverage body in the game here: three free proficiencies at 3 on top of Bard's own three, four Expertises by 10, and Peerless Skill at 14 adding an Inspiration die to your own check - usable in dialogue, which is a direct answer to the two-character coverage problem. Additional Magical Secrets at 6 reads a 221-spell pool four levels early and is what supplies Haste, Counterspell, Revivify or Fireball; that grant is the reason area, actions and both control axes clear rung 3. Cutting Words is a repeatable non-concentration rider on any enemy attack, check or damage roll. Light armour and no shield keep durability at 1.
uncertain: Cutting Words is now blocked by Silence, by Deafened targets and by Charm immunity (Goon), and how much of the Act II encounter set that removes is unverified.

bard/College of Swords (vanilla).why: The martial Bard: Extra Attack at 6, medium armour and scimitars at 3, a Fighting Style from a list UA Fighting Styles widens past Duelling and Two-Weapon Fighting, and six Flourishes. Four attacks a round with an Inspiration-die rider is about par, not ahead - the die is a short-rest pool, not a per-hit rider, until Master's Flourish at 14 lets a d6 stand in for free. Goon's interrupt versions of all three Flourishes convert Lone Wolf's spare reaction into damage. Medium armour is what lifts durability to par. Do not plan it around Arcane Acuity.
uncertain: Whether the Slashing Flourish's second target is frequent enough to move area above rung 2; scored as incidental.

bard/College of Valour (vanilla).why: The only College handing out shields plus martial weapons, which is the cheapest way to make a Charisma caster durable without a Fighter or Paladin dip - medium armour, a shield and Combat Inspiration's AC option put it a rung over par on durability. Extra Attack at 6 gives four attacks a round, about par on single-target with the Inspiration die as a short-rest rider. Battle Magic at 14 - a bonus-action weapon attack after casting a Bard spell - is the real action-economy gain, and it lands at the very top of Act II, after the character 12-13 judging point.
uncertain: Battle Magic at 14 sits inside Act II's band but after the 12-13 judging point; actions is scored without it.

bard/College of Glamour (vanilla).why: Mantle of Inspiration is bonus-action temp HP handed to the partner on a repeatable clock, and Mantle of Majesty at 6 is Command on tap - a no-concentration single-target control that lands every turn, which is what carries single-target control past the bare slot line. Unbreakable Majesty at 14 is the best single-target aggro-shed in the class and matters enormously in a two-body party, but it does not arrive until after the judging point, so durability is still the bare light-armour rung.
uncertain: Command as a repeatable no-concentration control is the Act I rung-4 clause; by Act II the rubric calls it background, so it was scored at 3, not 4.

bard/College of Eloquence.why: The strongest sustained Inspiration economy in the list. Unfailing Inspiration returns the die whenever an ally fails with it, which in a duo means the die is effectively free; Unsettling Words is a bonus-action, no-concentration save debuff whose die you see rolled before committing your control spell, which turns a coin-flip Hold Monster into a likely one. Silver Tongue treats a d20 of 9 or lower as a 10 on Persuasion and Deception - the largest single dialogue-gate lift in the roster if it works. Infectious Inspiration is 14 and lands after the judging point.
uncertain: The mod page's own Known Issues list says Silver Tongue is not working properly, possibly through Reliable Talent inheritance (bard.md:208-210). Skills 4 assumes it works; without it the rung is 3.

bard/College of Dance.why: A Dexterity martial Bard with no weapon proficiency and, critically, no Extra Attack - so it is two unarmed attacks a round plus one free Bardic Unarmed Kick after each Inspiration use, well under single-target par even with the damage die riding the Inspiration die to 1d10 at 10. Agile Strikes is the shape a duo wants (inspire the partner, get a free attack), but it is one attack a round, not a multiattack. Light armour, Dexterity-based, no shield. Inspiring Movement is a reaction ally buff on a once-per-round charge.
uncertain: Tandem Footwork, Improved Tandem Footwork and Leading Evasion are described only in images on the mod page (bard.md:256-260); Leading Evasion in particular could be a proportional durability layer, which would move durability a rung.

bard/College of Tragedy.why: A reaction-hungry College in a run where Lone Wolf grants a spare reaction, so Poetry in Misery (regain an Inspiration whenever anyone nearby rolls a natural 1) and Tale of Hubris (drop the crit threshold against a creature that crit you) can both be live in the same round - Poetry in Misery is genuine short-rest-economy relief. Sorrowful Fate converts any save the party forces into a Charisma save, which is a real single-target control rider, but it is not an interrupt and must be pre-cast on the target. Nimbus of Pathos at 14 is a fight-ending nuke that drops the target to 0 when it ends, which in a two-body party is 50% of the action economy.
uncertain: Feature names are matched from the Tal'Dorei source, not read from the pak (bard.md:280-282); the effects are verified, the names are not.
Nimbus of Pathos arrives at 14, after the judging point, and its downside makes it unscoreable as a straight buff regardless.

bard/College of Stormcalling.why: The only Bard College in the list that is a genuine blaster. Conductor holds concentration for 3d6 lightning and Shocked, and while it holds, Staccato Lightning is a bonus-action 2d6 plus Charisma against anything carrying an electrical or concussive status - two bonus actions a round makes that a real per-round engine rather than a rider. Chorus of Thunder inflicts Concussion (prone, no reactions, one action only) off a Bardic Inspiration, which is a short-rest pool. Electrifying Aria and Finale! are level 14 and land after the character 12-13 judging point.
uncertain: The lightning/thunder lock triggers Absolute Wrath's 0.5 multiplier on the resisted share; the slot pool is not locked, which is why area holds at 3.
Entered the list on a playtesting footing ('ADDED (for testing)'), so it is less battle-tested than the other Colleges.

bloodhunter/Order of the Ghostslayer.why: Brand of Sundering at 11 makes Crimson Rite roll two dice instead of one against a branded creature, which converts the class's flat 1d8 rider into something that outruns par - four attacks a round at about 1.20x. Curse Specialist front-loads a fourth Blood Maledict at level 3, one ahead of every other Order for the whole game, and drops the Bloodless restriction entirely, so the short-rest curse pool is the largest in the class. Blood Curse of the Exorcist at 15 is a two-body party's only reliable Charm/Fear break aimed outward. Crimson Rite is at-will with no clock, which is the rung-5 endurance shape by name.
uncertain: Aether Walk's intangibility is a per-short-rest escape rather than a mitigation layer; it was not scored into durability.
Rite Revival is level 18 and was not scored.

bloodhunter/Order of the Lycan.why: The highest raw damage in the class and the most durable body in this whole assignment. Hybrid Transformation stacks Resilient Hide's resistance to non-magical bludgeoning/piercing/slashing - a proportional layer, which does not decay - with +1 AC out of heavy armour and, from 11, Lycan Regeneration returning 1 plus Constitution every turn below half. Predatory Strikes scale off Dexterity and add a bonus-action unarmed strike, so Lone Wolf's two bonus actions take the swing count to six a round with the Rite on the fists. Heightened Senses is advantage on Perception, the hardest of the run's three recurring checks. Nothing aimed at the partner at all.
uncertain: Bloodlust - a Wisdom save at the start of any turn below half HP or lose control and attack the nearest creature - is a structural risk between 3 and 14 that no axis represents; it is exactly the failure a duo cannot absorb.
Unarmed damage (1d8 from 11) is lower per swing than a martial weapon; the rung rests on the extra instances, not the die.

bloodhunter/Order of the Mutant.why: Mutagencraft is the flexible pick: Celerity and Potency are +4 to a raw ability score at 11 and +5 at 18, and Listo removed the score cap, so they are a genuine stat rather than a rider. Cruelty grants an extra attack after any attack, which is what takes the swing count past four a round; Reconstruction returns proficiency-bonus HP a turn below half. Strange Metabolism's poison immunity at 7 is a large defensive swing given Listo's poison package. Every resistance mutagen hands out a matching vulnerability, which costs far more in a two-body party than a four-body one - Cruelty's is disadvantage on Int, Wis and Cha saves, which is the worst possible trade against this run's save load.
uncertain: Cruelty's disadvantage on Int/Wis/Cha saves cuts against the heaviest-weighted axis in the model and is not representable in the prof set; the durability and single-target rungs assume it is taken, which may be the wrong configuration.
Mutagens last until a rest, so only one configuration is live per fight - rule 3 requires a build-time pick and this profile names Celerity plus Reconstruction plus Cruelty.

bloodhunter/Order of the Profane Soul.why: The only Order that adds a caster axis and the only one that touches the duo's real gap. Brand of the Sapping Scar at 11 is blanket Disadvantage on the branded creature's saving throws, delivered by a free interrupt with no concentration - the rubric names it as the Act II rung-4 anchor on single-target control, and it never competes with the partner's one slot. Pact Magic off Intelligence with short-rest slots makes Hypnotic Pattern and Hunger of Hadar repeatable area answers on a clock a long rest does not gate. Mystic Frenzy turns a cantrip into a bonus-action weapon attack. The spell ceiling is level 4, so it never becomes a primary caster, and it needs real Intelligence investment for the DCs to matter.
uncertain: The patron choice moves rescue by two rungs - Celestial's Blood-Maledict healing reaches 3, most patrons reach 0-1; scored at 2 as a mid case rather than naming one.
Whether the Profane Soul patron list stacks correctly with a real Warlock level is unverified (listo-10.2-spells.md:530-531); immaterial to a mono-20 profile.
Dexterity rolls the attack while Intelligence drives the spell DC and Dark Augmentation, so the body needs two stats and cannot fund both to 22.

cleric/Heavy armour / martial weapon tab.why: cleric.md:148-175 is the dip-planning summary table listing which of the twenty domains grant heavy armour and martial weapons. It is a heading over a table, not a domain.

cleric/Death.why: Martial weapons but no heavy armour and no Extra Attack, so two attacks a round is half of par and the spell line scores better than the weapon line (~0.54x). Necrotic Divine Strike is a flat rider that par outruns. Control Undead off a Channel Divinity charge is the one real surplus - an enemy converted into a third body - but it competes with Turn Undead. Improved Reaper is a level-17 feature and does nothing in Act II.
uncertain: Whether Control Undead's converted body persists long enough per charge to read as a permanent extra body rather than a per-fight burst; scored as rung 2, not 3.

cleric/Knowledge.why: Light/medium only and no martial weapons, so the chassis is a plain full-caster body. What it buys is breadth: CCC's Magical Secrets at 6 and 10 pull from another class list, which is the only reason a Cleric reaches Fireball-grade area damage or Haste. Double proficiency in two of Arcana/History/Nature/Religion misses all three of the run's recurring checks, so skills reads 2, not high. Divine Foreknowledge is level 17.
uncertain: CCC's Magical Secrets pick count and source list are unverified on the mod page (cleric.md:197-198); aoe 3, ctrl 3 and act 2 all lean on it and would each drop a rung if the grant is narrower than assumed.

cleric/Life.why: The rescue ceiling of the list and nothing else on the Cleric table clears competent. Disciple of Life, Preserve Life off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge, and the base Cleric package of Revivify, Death Ward, Greater Restoration and Mass Healing Word give prevention plus restoration plus repeatable outward healing. Heavy armour and a shield put durability one rung over par; Blessed Healer's Goon fix routes its healing back to the caster, which is pool rather than rescue. Out-of-combat healing lifts endurance a rung above the bare 16-slot table.
uncertain: Whether Preserve Life's per-charge output is large enough at Cleric 12 to also carry durability; scored into rescue only, never both.

cleric/Light.why: Radiance of the Dawn is a short-rest area burst (~0.86x par on its own) sitting on top of Spirit Guardians, which is the only Cleric domain pair that reaches rung 3 on area without a domain Fireball. Potent Spellcasting makes the cantrip filler carry its weight. Warding Flare is the durability story: Lone Wolf's second reaction lets it impose disadvantage twice a round without giving up an opportunity attack, which is worth most on the boss hit. Corona of Light is level 17.
uncertain: Warding Flare's uptime against three crowd attacks a round - two reactions cover two of them, so the crowd half of the durability blend is only partly mitigated.

cleric/Nature.why: Heavy armour plus a shield, and the only domain with built-in Shillelagh access, which removes the feat tax on a Wisdom melee body - but with no Extra Attack it is still two attacks a round, well under par. Charm Animals and Plants is a short-rest area charm and is the reason area control clears rung 2. Master of Nature's third body is level 17 and does not exist in Act II.
uncertain: Listo moved Shillelagh to a level-1 spell, so whether the level-1 druid-cantrip picker still offers it is unverified (cleric.md:231-233); single-target is scored off the spell line regardless, so the rung does not move either way.

cleric/Tempest.why: Heavy armour and martial weapons, but no Extra Attack, so the swing count never reaches par. Destructive Wrath maximises thunder/lightning off a short-rest charge and the domain list carries Call Lightning, Sleet Storm and Ice Storm, so area damage and area control both clear rung 2. Wrath of the Storm is the repeatable non-concentration rider that lifts single-target control to 3. Absolute Wrath prices the lightning/thunder lock: the damage rungs already carry the 0.5 multiplier on the resisted share.
uncertain: How much of the encounter set actually resists lightning/thunder from Act II; the ratio was taken at the rubric's assumed half.

cleric/Trickery.why: The weakest chassis of the eight vanilla domains and the Listo BotT buff mod is not installed. No heavy armour, no martial weapons, no damage rider worth naming. Invoke Duplicity's single duplicate is the only surplus above the Lone Wolf floor before level 17, where Improved Duplicity's four decoys finally become real action economy - outside Act II.
uncertain: Whether a single Invoke Duplicity decoy soaks enough attacks to read as an extra body (rung 2) or merely as a rider (rung 1).

cleric/War.why: The only domain with true Extra Attack (CCC at 6), and War Priest stacks a bonus-action attack on top of it. Four attacks a round plus roughly half a War Priest charge per round and a Divine Strike rider lands at about 0.98x par - par, not ahead, because Cleric weapon damage carries no scaling rider. Multiattack plus a recurring bonus-action attack is squarely rung 3 on actions. Heavy armour and a shield hold durability at one rung over par.
uncertain: War Priest charges are long-rest (6 at Cleric 11), so only about two land per hard fight; the damage ratio was amortized on that, not on the headline six.

cleric/Arcana.why: The only domain that gives a Cleric native Counterspell, which in a duo has no other holder and which Lone Wolf's spare reaction pays for. Arcane Abjuration banishes off a short-rest charge with no concentration, and that plus the base Hold Person line is what carries single-target control to 3. No armour or weapon grant at all, so the body is a plain caster on medium and a shield. Arcane Mastery is level 17.
uncertain: Arcane Abjuration's banish threshold keys off target level (CR 2 at Cleric 11, 3 at 14), so how many Act II enemies it actually reaches is unverified; single-target control would fall to 2 if the answer is few.

cleric/Forge.why: The most durable Cleric chassis: heavy armour plus a shield plus Soul of the Forge's +1 AC in heavy, plus fire resistance and a permanent +1 AC or +1 attack/damage buff renewed every long rest. That is roughly AC 20 and a proportional layer on one damage type - ahead of par but short of a general resistance, since Saint of Forge and Fire's physical resistance is level 17. Sleight of Hand is a real skills grant here: it is the roll behind the Araj pickpocket and the Act III Phalar Aluve gate.
uncertain: Whether Blessing of the Forge's +1 AC composes with attuned defensive gear or is overwritten; scored as composing.

cleric/Grave.why: Sentinel at Death's Door is the best defensive feature on the Cleric table for a duo - it turns a critical hit against you or your partner into an ordinary hit, Wisdom-modifier times per long rest, off the reaction Lone Wolf leaves spare. That is prevention aimed outward, which is the rung-4 clause, and Revivify plus Raise Dead plus Death Ward on the domain list complete the rung-5 set. Light/medium only, so durability rides Sentinel rather than armour. Path to the Grave's vulnerability window is a damage enabler for the partner, not control.
uncertain: Sentinel is scored entirely into rescue; the share of it that protects this body rather than the partner was not double-counted into durability, which may understate durability by a rung.

cleric/Order.why: The single best action-economy domain in a two-player run: Voice of Authority turns every level-1-or-higher spell aimed at your partner into a free weapon attack from them, every turn, at no resource cost. That is an action handed to the other body on a repeatable clock, which is what separates rung 4 from rung 3. Order's Demand is a short-rest area charm that also disarms, and the domain list carries Hold Person, Slow, Compulsion and Dominate Person. Heavy armour and a shield. Order's Wrath is level 17.
uncertain: Voice of Authority grants an attack, not a full Action, so rung 5's literal clause is not met; scored at 4.

cleric/Peace.why: Emboldening Bond is a pair-scope save booster - +1d4 to every attack, check and save on both bodies, permanently online in a duo - and that is the domain's real product. Protective Bond is damage redirection, which in a two-body party moves damage from one half of the party to the other and is capped at rung 1 on its own; it is recorded as the booster and as a pair flag, not as rescue above the base Cleric package. Light/medium only, the weakest armour of the strong domains. Warding Bond at Peace 3 is the Cleric's only route to the spell.
uncertain: Whether Protective Bond's carrier-doubling belongs in this body's durability rung; scoring-model.md applies it at pair scope, so it was left out of the base profile.

cleric/Twilight.why: Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action outward temp-HP tap that fires on every creature's turn end for one Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds - roughly 1d6+12 a round on both bodies at character 12. That is the rung-4 rescue clause, and Aura of Vitality, Aura of Life, Death Ward and Greater Restoration on top of the base Cleric list complete rung 5. The same temp HP is what carries durability to 4 on a heavy-armour-plus-shield body. Heavy armour and martial weapons, but no Extra Attack, so damage stays under par.
uncertain: Twilight Sanctuary's temp HP is scored into this body's pool and into outward rescue; the rubric forbids scoring the same feature twice, but the aura genuinely lands on both bodies, so it was counted once each way rather than twice one way.

cleric/Strength (Rhonas).why: The only Cleric domain with Haste on its own list, and Haste on the partner is the largest action-economy lever a two-person party has. Heavy armour but no martial weapons, an odd gap, and no Extra Attack, so the weapon line never reaches par. Avatar of Battle II adds non-magical physical resistance during a three-turn transform, two charges per long rest - real but too thin a clock to carry durability past one rung over par.
uncertain: Whether the level-1 druid cantrip can still pick Shillelagh after Listo moved it to a level-1 spell (cleric.md:418-420).

cleric/Zeal (Hazoret).why: Heavy armour, martial weapons and Priest of Zeal's bonus-action attack from level 1, plus Haste and Fireball on the domain list - the only Cleric domain carrying both. Consuming Fervor maximises fire or thunder off a Channel Divinity charge, which the rubric prices at about 1.29x area par in Act II, and Fireball off ordinary slots stacks on that, so area clears rung 3. Priest of Zeal is Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest, so only about two land per fight and the swing count still falls short of single-target par. Endurance is a rung up because the damage engine is the short-rest charge.
uncertain: Blaze of Glory is level 17 and was not scored. The fire/thunder lock is priced at the rubric's assumed half-resisted share.

cleric/Inquisition.why: Heavy armour and martial weapons, and Listo's own changelog flags it as expected top-tier. Spell Shield is the standout: a bonus action giving a creature 1d10+level temp HP that carries spell-damage resistance and advantage on saves against spells while it holds - in a duo one charge covers half the team. Witch Hunter's Strike is Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest and does not stack with the Divine Strike interrupt, so the damage rider is smaller than it reads. Banishment, Silence and Dominate Person on the domain list carry single-target control to 3.
uncertain: Spell Shield is scored into rescue, not into this body's saves; whether self-targeting it should lift durability was left unscored to avoid double-counting.

cleric/Eldritch.why: Prophecy of Doom is the widest crowd control on the Cleric table from one short-rest Channel Divinity charge - every creature in a 5m sphere at 27m rolls a Wisdom save against a random Eldritch Effect for a minute, and the best entries ('move or act, not both, no reactions') are a direct action-economy tax. Eldritch Contagion is a bonus-action, no-concentration single-target rider that fires off every levelled cast. Unpredictable Inspiration's free re-selectable skill proficiency is worth a real rung on the untelegraphed Perception/Investigation load. No armour grant.
uncertain: Both control features roll from a random effect table, several entries of which are weak or actively helpful to the enemy; both rungs were cut one below the shape of the feature to price that.

cleric/Night.why: Invocation of Night is slot-free area control on a short-rest clock: it blinds every enemy in 9m that fails a Constitution save for rounds equal to Cleric level, and extinguishes magical light on the way. Ward of Shadows is Warding Flare's pattern - a reaction imposing disadvantage, and Lone Wolf leaves a reaction spare for it - which is what lifts durability over par on a light/medium body. Sleep's +14 HP of effect at 8 with a critical-hit rider is a genuine second area answer.
uncertain: Ward of Shadows fails against enemies that cannot be Blinded, and how large that population is in Listo's encounter set is unverified.

cleric/Dream.why: Deep Slumber plus Torpor is hard area control from level 1 - a Torpored enemy gets one of attack, action or bonus action, quarter movement and no reactions - and Hypnotic Pattern, Fear, Confusion and Synaptic Static sit above it on the domain list. Inception makes the first save against every Int- or Wis-save spell roll at disadvantage, which is the rider that stacks with the DC rather than depending on it. Mind Sliver as a Wisdom-based Cleric cantrip carries a save penalty on the filler action. No armour or weapon grant.
uncertain: The DTO page carries no bonus-proficiency list for the domain, so light/medium and no martial weapons is inferred, not read (cleric.md:532-533). Inception consumes the Channel Divinity charge on cast, so it competes with nothing else the domain wants - but the charge count (2 at Cleric 6) caps it at about two casts a fight.

druid/Circle of the Land.why: Natural Recovery is the only in-combat-day slot refund in the class, and at druid 13 that is 5-7 slot levels back per short rest - roughly half the pool again across a cycle, which is what carries end to 4 in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies. Everything else is the base druid: medium armour and shield sits exactly on the durability par anchor, Conjure Animals made non-concentration until long rest by 13458 plus Flock of Familiars is a multi-body summon set under Automated Summons, and the 117-spell prepared list carries the area axes.
uncertain: Land type is a build-time pick (rule 3) and the circle spell pair at 3/5/7/9 varies with it; scored on the list-average rather than a named land.
Nature's Ward at 10 (poison and disease immunity, no charm or fright from elementals and fey) has no id in the booster registry, so it is recorded here rather than in boosters.
Exact vanilla-circle progression at 13-20 is flagged unverified in the class file; the Act II judgement point of character 12-13 is inside the verified band.

druid/Circle of the Moon.why: Wild Shape as a second HP bar, entered as a bonus action twice per short rest with CR3 forms from 9, plus Lunar Mend: the pool ratio runs past 2.2x par before the beast form's lower AC pulls it back to roughly 1.8, which is a durable chassis rather than a par one. It adds no body - it makes the one body hard to remove, which is the right trade when losing either character ends the fight. Damage stays the caster's, because beast-form attacks carry no gear and no scaling.
uncertain: Beast-form damage collects no gear constant at all, which is why st stays at the caster figure rather than the wild-shape one; if the Wild Shape Overhaul carries item bonuses into beast form, st is understated.
The class file records that the level 10 second Extra Attack is gone under WSO.
concentration is false because BG3 does not permit casting in beast form and the Moon plan is spent there; a Moon druid that stays out of form reads true.

druid/Circle of the Spores.why: The only druid whose melee routine beats its casting: 4018's real Extra Attack works outside Wild Shape, Shillelagh puts Wisdom on both attack and damage, and Symbiotic Entity adds 1d6 a hit plus 4 temp HP per druid level (52 at 13). Halo of Spores fires on both Lone Wolf reactions at doubled damage, so the instance count is six a round against par's four, which is where the gear constant does its work. Fungal Infestation adds four bodies a long rest on top of Conjure Animals and the circle's own Animate Dead, and none of it holds concentration.
uncertain: Both 4018 and the Wild Shape Overhaul 1148 rewrite the level 5 and 10 attack features; the class file flags that this resolves to exactly one Extra Attack as unverified. Two Extra Attacks would push st to 4.

Dealer's Choice lets Acid, Necrotic and Poison be picked independently per feature; scored with acid or a mix so rule 4's 0.5 resistance multiplier does not bite. A pure-Poison configuration would take st and aoe down a rung without Elemental Adept.
Spreading Spores at 10 was scored into aoe alongside the spell pool rather than separately.

druid/Circle of the Stars.why: Star Druid Tweaks moves Cosmic Omen onto a short rest, so 3-4 swings of plus-or-minus 1d6 on saves or attacks are affordable three times a long-rest cycle - Woe on an enemy save is the repeatable non-concentration rider that carries ctrl_s, Weal is save-or-die insurance. Archer's bonus-action Luminous Arrow fires on both Lone Wolf bonus actions for 2d8+Wis radiant, and Chalice turns every healing spell into a free extra 2d8+Wis outward, which is a no-action rescue rider. Twinkling Constellations at 10 makes all three forms live in the same turn.
uncertain: Whether Luminous Arrow and Dazzling Breath can each be used twice a round on Lone Wolf's two bonus actions, or are once-per-turn, is the difference between st 3 and st 2.
Dragon form's concentration floor (treat rolls of 9 or lower as 10) is a real concentration defence but has no id in the booster registry and is not a saving throw proficiency; recorded here.

druid/Circle of the Sea.why: Evard's Black Tentacles at circle 7 and Sleet Storm at 5 are the rubric's own Act II rung-5 area-denial examples, always prepared, on top of the base druid list - the deepest area control in the class. Crashing Wave is a bonus-action Nd6 cold where N is the Wisdom modifier (6d6 at Wis 22) plus a 5m push every turn the current is up, which is both a damage engine and a repeatable non-concentration peel. Stormborn at 10 adds Cold, Lightning and Thunder resistance plus flight while it runs.
uncertain: Whether Crashing Wave can fire on both Lone Wolf bonus actions is not stated; st 3 assumes two uses a round and drops to 2 at one.
Crashing Wave is scored as save-negates (x0.55); if it is save-for-half the damage rises by about 40 percent.
Oceanic Gift at 14 - projecting the current onto the partner - is Act III and is excluded, though it is the feature the class file calls the circle's duo argument.

druid/Circle of Stormchasers.why: Storm Shift buys 3x druid level in temp HP (39 at 13) plus Wisdom added to every Lightning, Thunder or Cold damage roll, for one Wild Shape charge lasting until long rest and holding no concentration. Level 10 makes those three types ignore Resistance and treat Immunity as Resistance, which is the clean escape from rule 4's 0.5 multiplier that an elemental build in a two-body party otherwise has no answer to. Storm's Reach adds a bonus-action proficiency-bonus-worth of d8s, five times a long rest.
uncertain: Storm's Reach's damage table is locked at the level 12 value and will not scale past 12, so it is already frozen at the Act II judgement point and slides through Act III.
st computes to about 1.15x par, exactly on the rung 2/3 boundary; 3 was taken because the +Wis rider lands on every instance rather than once per spell.
Level 14's resistance and free Chain Lightning are Act III.

druid/Circle of Winter.why: Level 10 makes anything that fails a save against a Cold-damage druid spell fall Prone - area hard control riding on damage the body was casting anyway, costing no extra action and no concentration, under a circle list of Sleet Storm, Ice Storm, Cone of Cold and Snilloc's. Winter Spirit is the largest temp-HP number in the class at 5 per druid level (65 at 13) and adds Wisdom as bonus Cold damage to every damage-dealing druid spell, not merely cold ones, plus 1d6 on melee - the author's own Shillelagh pairing.
uncertain: The Winter Spirit bonus damage explicitly does not itself count as a Cold-damage spell for the Prone trigger, so the level 10 rider only fires on spells that already deal cold; ctrl_a 5 assumes the circle list supplies enough of those, which it does from level 5.

Winter Spirit ends when its temp HP runs out, so the damage rider and the durability layer share one resource and cannot both be counted at full value - dur was scored on the temp HP, st on the rider, and st came out at 1.07x par, rung 2.
Level 14 Cold immunity is Act III.

druid/Circle of Dreams.why: Balm of the Summer Court spends half a druid-level-sized d6 pool in one bonus action at 18m for Nd6 + Wisdom of healing and matching temp HP - six dice at 13 - and Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow, once per short rest, makes every one of those dice roll maximum. Hidden Paths at 10 is a bonus-action extraction for the partner, Wisdom-modifier uses. Prevention, restoration off the base list's Revivify and Greater Restoration, and repeatable outward healing that costs a bonus action rather than an Action: the whole rescue ladder at once.
uncertain: All three resources replenish on a long rest only (ReplenishType Rest on SummerCourtDie, HiddenPath and DreamsWalkerPoint), which is why end stayed at 3 despite the pool's size.
Walker in Dreams at 14 - a free short rest plus all 1st and 2nd level slots back once per long rest - is Act III and is excluded; it is worth real supplies at 120 per camp.
The Balm pool is fungible between self and partner; it is booked entirely to rsc, since the rubric forbids scoring one feature on both dur and rsc.

druid/Circle of the Shepherd.why: Every totem is an aura aimed at the other body: Bear hands the partner 5 + druid level in temp HP with no action spent after the summon, Flumph makes every healing spell also heal them for your druid level, Frog and Wolf hand out advantage on Dexterity saves and on attacks. Mighty Summoner then makes the base list's Conjure Animals, Flock of Familiars and Find Familiar ignore all resistance to physical damage on unarmed attacks, which is quality on top of a body count the base druid already has.
uncertain: Only one Spirit Totem exists at a time, so rule 3 forced a pick; rsc 4 is scored on Bear's no-action outward temp HP, and a Flumph configuration trades that for healing amplification without changing the rung.

druid/Circle of Wildfire.why: A permanent extra body that casts your spells from its own position - a second point of origin for area damage, which a two-body party otherwise cannot generate, and the reason Enhanced Bond is worth more here than in a four-party. Warden of Life at circle 7 is prevention on the partner alongside Revivify at 5 and Mass Cure Wounds at 9, and Blazing Revival is an automatic second life on the body itself, which is Durability rather than Rescue.
uncertain: Exact levels for Cauterizing Flames and Blazing Revival are unverified (5e puts them at 6 and 14); if Blazing Revival is a level 14 feature it is Act III and dur drops to 2.
Blazing Revival requires the Wildfire Spirit to activate it on its own turn rather than firing instantly, so it is not a reliable layer.
Cauterizing Flames must be activated on your turn because Reactions did not work for it, and Misty Step is among the spells excluded from casting through the spirit.

druid/Circle of Wrath.why: A self-contained scaling damage engine with no summon and no gear dependency: two aspects at 2 and a third at 10, each a scaling cantrip that builds Wrath stacks up to the Wisdom modifier for +1 spell damage each, cashed out through Revelations once per Wild Shape charge. The type spread is the real asset - Fulminate is force and Consecrate Wrath is radiant, the two least-resisted types in the list, so rule 4's 0.5 multiplier never lands.

monk/Way of the Open Hand (vanilla).why: Extra Attack plus double Flurry is eight instances a round for 1.33x par, and Open Hand Technique hangs Topple, Push or Stagger on every one of those strikes for no ki, no action and no concentration, on the Ki Save DC the build already funds Wisdom for. monk/Way of the Ascendant Dragon.why: Breath of the Dragon replaces one attack of the Attack action with a cone at three Martial Arts dice from 11, so Lone Wolf's two Actions deliver two breaths a round net of the replaced attacks - real area damage from a class that has none. Aspect of the Wyrm at 11 is the only Way that hands the partner a defensive buff, an elemental resistance aura on a bonus action.

monk/Way of the Astral Self.why: The single-stat Monk: the arms roll attack and damage off Wisdom in Force, so the 22 sits on the stat that also drives AC and the Ki Save DC and Dexterity and Strength can both stay low with the points going to Constitution. Deflect Energy at 11 reduces six damage types by 1d10+Wis per reaction, and Lone Wolf's second reaction makes this the best user of that extra reaction in the class.

Requires Script Extender for the Wisdom attack conversion.
Awakened Astral Self's third attack and +2 AC land at 17, in Act III.

monk/Way of the Kensei.why: Sharpen the Blade is up to +3 attack and damage on the kensei weapon for a minute (three ki, and rule 1's mundane weapon carries no enchantment to block it), Deft Strike adds a Martial Arts die once per turn, and the two together take the eight-instance Monk routine past 1.5x par. Innate Mastery's +2 to attack and damage is the only unconditional damage grant in the six.

Radiant Soul adds Cha to radiant or fire only, so it does not touch the Force blast engine.

warlock/The Psyker.why: Warp Wielder both applies and shortens Warp, so three beams on one target detonate inside the same Action: 87 in beams plus 54 in detonations is 141 = 1.62x par, in Force, at no action, slot or concentration cost, and the same beams spread across a crowd put a 3 m explosion on each. Perils of the Warp charges max HP per beam on an accumulating stack with only a level-10 short-rest brake, which is why Durability and Endurance both drop rather than one of them.
uncertain: The class file's own load-bearing assumption - that a duration driven to 0 detonates in-turn - decides st 4 versus st 3 (1.31x); worth one combat log.

Perils' MultiplyEffectsByDuration arithmetic taken literally zeroes max HP in round 2; Durability is scored 1 rather than 0 on the assumption it is floored somewhere, and this is the single largest uncertainty in this set.
The Warp level map carries a PreferredClassUUID, so Warlock-level versus character-level keying is unverified.
Repulsor and Silence in the Perils random table do not exclude the partner; friendly fire is not priced on any axis here.

wizard/Abjuration.why: Full-caster pool reads 0.85x st par and the rubric's stated 2.00x aoe par at Act II; Arcane Ward (cap 2x level, +level per short rest from 10) is the only school that lifts a d6 robe body's eHP to par, and Projected Ward is repeatable outward prevention on a short-rest clock spent through Lone Wolf's spare reaction.
uncertain: Whether the ward loses one charge per hit or charges equal to damage absorbed changes its eHP contribution by roughly a factor of two.
Spell Resistance is Expansion at 14, so it is an Act III grant and is excluded from these Act II rungs.

wizard/Bladesinging.why: Light armour plus Bladesong's +4 AC at wizard 9 puts AC near 19-21 and Song of Defence (10) buys 5 flat reduction per slot level, which prices out ahead of par against Act II's 9.6 crowd hit; Extra Attack at 6 makes the filler action worth roughly 27 instead of a 16.5 cantrip, which holds st at par rather than raising it.
uncertain: Song of Victory (+Int to weapon damage) is Expansion at 14 and therefore Act III; it is excluded here.
Bladesong is a long-rest resource (3 uses at wizard 5, 4 at 9), so uptime across three hard fights is assumed near-total but not verified.

wizard/Conjuration.why: Focused Conjuration at 10 makes summon concentration undroppable by damage and the level-6 off-list picks reach the druid/cleric summon pool, which is a multi-body summon set rather than the base list's single Animate Dead; the bonus-action item conjurer adds a short-rest damage instance and small healing potions the partner can drink.
uncertain: The mod places its features at 3 and 6 against vanilla's 2 and 6; whether the level-2 slot is replaced or supplemented is unverified in the class file.
Small healing potions as outward healing are scored at rung 2; their size is not stated.

wizard/Divination.why: Portent is slot-free hard control on a short-rest clock once Expert Divination's Prophecies refund the dice at 6 - three dice spent through Lone Wolf's second reaction convert a boss save into a guaranteed failure without touching the concentration slot, which is the rung-4 clause on ctrl_s. Dice spent on an enemy attack roll instead are a small eHP layer.
uncertain: Greater Portent at 14 is listed in Expansion's changelog but flagged uncertain in the class file; it is Act III regardless.
The dice pool is fungible between control and durability, so both cannot be spent at once; ctrl_s is scored as the primary use.

wizard/Enchantment.why: Hypnotic Gaze is single-target charm-and-incapacitate maintainable every turn that explicitly does not hold your concentration (22655 makes it break the target's instead), which is the rung-4 no-concentration clause; Split Enchantment at 10 doubles Hold Monster and Dominate Person off the same slot at exactly the level encounters field pairs of dangerous bodies.
uncertain: Hypnotic Gaze is a long-rest recharge, not a short-rest one, which is why this stops at 4 rather than the rung-5 short-rest clause.

The class file warns Listo enemies are far more save-capable and bosses carry magic resistance; the rubric holds that save-DC control does not decay, so no rung was deducted, but the two claims are in tension.

wizard/Evocation.why: Empowered Evocation adds Int to each damage roll, lifting the half-pool area ratio from the rubric's 2.00 to roughly 2.3 - real but inside the same band - and Sculpt Spells is worth more in a duo than in a four-party because the partner is always inside the fireball, so it is the one school that can actually field the whole-pool area configuration without friendly fire. No layer outside damage, so the rest of the vector is the bare wizard's.
uncertain: Whether Empowered Evocation's Int bonus applies once per spell or once per target materially changes the aoe ratio; per-target was assumed and still lands inside rung 4.
Overchannel is Expansion at 14 and therefore Act III.

wizard/Illusion.why: The thinnest of the base schools: a bonus-action Minor Illusion, a short-rest See Invisibility and one negated attack per rest at 10 add nothing that moves a rung off the shared spell list. Every value here is the bare wizard chassis.
uncertain: Illusory Self negates one attack per rest; against an Act II boss hit of 28.8 that is real but far short of the roughly 15 percent eHP a rung costs.
The class file says Listo's enemy overhaul makes Minor Illusion's pull far less reliable than vanilla, so no ctrl_a credit was taken for it.

wizard/Necromancy.why: Animate Dead++ removes the undead cap entirely, moves the free cast to 5 and upcasts two more bodies per slot above 5th, and Undead Thralls hands all of them wizard-level HP and proficiency to damage - the largest body count in the list, non-concentration and until long rest, which is the rung-5 Actions clause. Inured to Undeath at 10 adds necrotic resistance and blanks Act II's max-HP reduction.
uncertain: Summons are excluded from st and aoe by the rubric's rule 2, so the undead show up only on act; whether the pair-level Actions cap then re-clips them is scoring-model business, not this profile's.
concentration is false because the undead plan itself holds no slot, though most builds would still run one control spell.

wizard/Transmutation.why: Transmuter's Stone at 6 is the cheapest Constitution-save proficiency in the class and is the rare cross-character item a Wizard can simply leave equipped on the partner; Experimental Alchemy brewing two solutions per check is out-of-combat healing supply, which the Endurance budget counts directly.
uncertain: The four stone variants are mutually exclusive and only one exists at a time; prof records the Constitution-save variant per rule 3's one-configuration requirement, but a build that hands the stone to the partner or picks the resistance variant does not hold it.
Experimental Alchemy does not stack with Artificer or feat sources, and the feat version was removed in 9.0.3.

wizard/War Magic.why: A reaction-based AC and save spike on a body that holds a second reaction from Lone Wolf, plus an initiative bonus and a once-per-turn force rider on a spell; the defensive reaction is the only thing that lifts a robe chassis off dur 1, and force is the least-resisted type in the list.
uncertain: The class file states outright that Arcane Deflection, Tactical Wit, Power Surge and Durable Magic numbers are unverified - the mod page tables are images. Every value above is scored on the feature shape, not on magnitudes.
Arcane Deflection's save bonus has no id in the booster registry, so it is recorded here rather than in boosters.
Whether the level-2 and level-6 optional homebrew variants are enabled changes the package; the base variants were assumed.

wizard/Order of Scribes.why: Formulaic Attunement is the list's cleanest resistance strip, which matters because rule 4's 0.5 multiplier on a resisted type is the one thing that can halve a caster's damage from Act II; it also adds a small flat bonus on the attuned type. The Spectral Mind is a remote casting position rather than an attacker.
uncertain: Levels for Wizardly Quill and Awakened Spellbook and the exact Formulaic Attunement damage bonus are unverified - the mod page tables are images.
Casting through the Spectral Mind is a genuine survivability tool that the effective-HP ratio in section 3 cannot express, so dur may be understated at 1.
One With The Word at 14 is Act III.

wizard/Hexcraft.why: Four Eldritch Invocations by wizard 10, unrestricted by pact, on top of Warlock spells copied into the spellbook - Armour of Shadows and Fiendish Vigor are at-will AC and temp HP that cost no slot, and the ritual temp-HP engine at 6 (ritual level + wizard level) refreshes before every fight given Listo's Ritual Caster teaches every ritual on the list. Immunity to the whole charm and fear line at 10 is worth a great deal when losing either body ends the run.
uncertain: Whether invocations retain their Warlock-level prerequisites is not stated; Chains of Carceri (Warlock 12) would be a rung-5 ctrl_s clause if reachable, and ctrl_s 4 assumes the no-concentration invocation tier is reachable but Carceri is not.
Whether Eldritch Blast itself is copyable as a cantrip - and therefore whether Agonising Blast is live - is unverified, and it would move both damage axes.
Level-10 charm and fear immunity has no id in the booster registry, so it is recorded here rather than in boosters.
Heart of Darkness at 14 is Act III.

wizard/Hierophant.why: The only Wizard that clears the whole rescue ladder at once: Erudite Remedy is a bonus-action outward heal that also hands the partner a chosen elemental resistance until your next turn (prevention), Lesser and Greater Restoration are always prepared at 3 and 9, and Miracleworker at 10 makes Raise Dead a ritual. Spirit Guardians on an Intelligence caster is a real area floor and the remedy pool doubles as out-of-combat healing, which the Endurance budget counts.
uncertain: The remedy pool is one pool; the rubric forbids scoring the same feature on dur and rsc, so it is booked entirely to rsc and dur is left at the bare robe value of 1.
Warding Rejuvenation at 14 is Act III and is excluded.

wizard/School of Death.why: Touch of Death converts two Arcane Recovery charges into 5 + twice wizard level necrotic (31 at 13, about four uses a long rest), Negative Energy Infusion adds 1d8 once per turn on a spell attack, and Inescapable Destruction strips necrotic resistance so rule 4's 0.5 multiplier never lands on the list's most commonly resisted type. Reaper doubling single-target necrotic cantrips makes the filler action worth two instances. No defensive layer whatsoever, and it pays for its damage out of Arcane Recovery, which is the Endurance pool.
uncertain: The st ratio computes to roughly 1.0-1.2x Act II par depending on how the levelled half of the pool is spent, straddling the 2/3 boundary; 3 was taken because the class file states this is the highest sustained single-target of the schools and because the conservative per-cast figure was already at 1.01.
Improved Reaper at 14 is Act III.

wizard/School of Bombardment.why: Arcane Ordnance refills its single charge on any spell cast, so with two Actions the routine is spell-then-bomb every round: a slot-free three-dice-plus-Int area attack that lays its own persistent surface, which is exactly the no-concentration repeatable area-denial clause, stacked under the wizard's own Evard's and Hypnotic Pattern. The bomb is also a genuine at-will floor, so no round is spent on a bare cantrip.
uncertain: DEFECT recorded in the class file: Salvo (6) and Barrage (10) require 2 and 3 Bombs charges and nothing in the pak grants more than 1, so both were scored as unreachable. If some other mod raises the ceiling, aoe is understated by at least a rung.

Whether a bomb itself counts as a spell for the refill is unverified and is load-bearing here - it is the difference between one bomb per spell cast and one every turn; the ctrl_a 5 and end 3 assume the routine above works.
Saturating Fire at 14 is Act III.
